messages.author: d27197bd30d0e710
messages.subject: incorrect date tick labels
parts:
Hello,

I'm using ggplot to visualize time series data and I noticed that
sometimes the tick labels are incorrectly computed. I search on the
web to see if this problem is documented but didn't find anything
relevant.

I was able to get a small repro shown below. If you run it it will
show four labels Dec-10, Jan-11, Feb-11 and March-11 on the x-axis but
if you find the text annotation for March 11 data point you'll notice
that it doesn't align with the tick mark.

dates <- seq(as.Date("2010-11-10"), as.Date("2011-03-13"), "days")
f <- data.frame(date = dates, position = 1:length(dates) %% 3)
ggplot(f, aes(x = date, y = position)) +
geom_text(aes(label = as.character(date)), angle = 90) +
geom_vline(aes(xintercept = date), alpha = 0.2)

What am I missing here? Is this a bug or did misunderstood the
fundamentals of how ggplot labels axes with dates.

Thank you,
David

messages.author: d27197bd30d0e710
messages.subject: Re: incorrect date tick labels
parts:
You're right, this is the reason! It's another piece of empirical
evidence that (my) IQ drops a lot under stress ;)

Still, the dash in the format makes this confusing. If you shorten the
date range, the format changes automatically to %dd-%MM (for example,
range 2011-02-10 - 2011-03-13, will produce labels 14-Feb, 21-Feb...)
but add a few days and the format changes to %MM-%YY... giving Dec-10,
Jan-11 which looks almost the same...

I'm not sure if this is locale specific, but I'd recommend removing
the dash in the latter case or adding a full year. I realize, I can
change it myself but the defaults will be used by many people.

Thanks!
